Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make an inquiry concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The Investment Policy Advisory Committee is a new committee, effective July 1, 2017. With the City Treasurer, the Committee shall be responsible for recommending investment brokers, proposing changes to investment policy and practices, presenting investment reports, and evaluating and recommending banking-related matters. Meetings are to review, discuss and develop recommendation on matters such as investment and banking vendors, policy, transactions, returns and performance, brokers, and strategy.
The Investment Policy Advisory Committee, at the direction of the Chairman with concurrence of the Committee, may modify the order of items shown on the agenda.
This meeting will be held via videoconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID- 19 and pursuant to the Governor's Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-20 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer's Safer at Home Order (revised March 21, 2020). MINUTES
  OF THE MAY 18, 2021 SPECIAL MEETING
  OF THE INVESTMENT POLICY ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA 90274

A Teleconference meeting of the Palos Verdes Estates Investment Policy Advisory Committee
special meeting via Zoom pursuant to Executive Order N25-20 issued by Governor Gavin
Newsom on March 26, 2020, was called to order by Chair Greenberg at 4:01 P.M. on May 18,
2021, notice having been given with affidavit thereto on file. Members of the public were
provided with the following information to provide public input:

  BY COMPUTER: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/85719586756
  Zoom Meeting ID: 857 1958 6756
  BY TELEPHONE: 1 669 900 9128, Enter Code: 857 1958 6756#
  BY EMAIL: CityCouncilMeeting@pvestates.org

CALL TO ORDER 4:01 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PRESENT: Chair Greenberg, Members Murdock, and DeLarme

ALSO PRESENT:
Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi, Finance Analyst Smith, Consultant Cole

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

ACTION: Moved by Member DeLarme, seconded by Member Murdock to approve the agenda.
AYES: Greenberg, DeLarme, Murdock
NOES: None
RESULT: Motion Passed

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

The following individuals addressed the Investment Policy Advisory Committee: Consultant Cole,
Finance Analyst Smith, and Patrick Jones
 NEW AND OLD BUSINESS

1.  Appointment of a Secretary Pro Tempore of the Investment Policy Advisory
  Committee

  Recommendation Action: Adopt a Motion appointing Erin Smith, Finance Analyst, as
  Secretary Pro Tempore of the Investment Policy Advisory Committee.

  ACTION: Moved by Member DeLarme, seconded by Member Murdock to Appoint
  Erin Smith, Finance Analyst, as Secretary Pro Tempore of the Investment Policy
  Advisory Committee.
  AYES: Greenberg, DeLarme, and Murdock
  NOES: None
  RESULT: Motion Passed

2.  Verbal Report from the Section 115 Trust Ad-Hoc Subcommittee (Members Jeff
  DeLarme and Bob Murdock)

  Recommendation Action: Receive a Verbal Presentation from the Section 115 Trust Ad-
  Hoc Subcommittee, Discuss the Subject of a Section 115 Trust, and Make Any
  Recommendation to the City Council as Deemed Appropriate.

  Members DeLarme and Murdock presented.

  The Subcommittee Members were tasked with exploring cities that have created Section
  115 Trusts. Member DeLarme spoke to representatives from Culver City, El Segundo,
  Camarillo, and received a referral from Beverly Hills in regards to their Section 115
  Trust. The cities were in favor of or had positive feedback of the adoption of their
  Section 115 Trust. Member DeLarme was encouraged by these representatives to talk
  to more cities about their experiences. He received no negative feedback so far, and he
  recommended the City should explore the subject further.

  Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi asked how the Section 115 Trusts get used, managed, and funded.
  Member DeLarme responded that the cities used PARS to manage the funds and use
  unrestricted funds to fund the Trust. Member Murdock spoke to Berkeley, Beverly Hills,
  and Manhattan Beach. Berkeley put a lump sum of $10 million in Pension Stability
  Trust. Beverly Hills put $23 million into PARS Conservative Fund. Manhattan Beach
  put $1.4 million into PARS Moderate Fund, then switched to PARS Moderately
  Conservative Fund. Then City staff recommended to close the fund in 2019. The Fund
  was closed because of its small size ($1.4 million), the cost of administration, and
  because of the general underperformance of the Trust compared to CalPERS. Member
  Murdock continued: If operating this Trust conservatively with a short window, you’re
  only taking 40% of the risk of a CalPERS portfolio. If CalPERS is expecting 7%, you’re
  expecting the Trust to earn 2.8% minus fees, 60 basis points, 2.2% expected return.
 Manhattan Beach wasn’t happy with the underperformance relative to CalPERS.
Member Murdock mentioned a small fund size of $1.4 million is probably not worth
while going through the paperwork of setting-up a Trust. If the choice is send the money
directly to CalPERS or put it in a 115 Trust, you’re giving up 60% of your return by
putting money in the Trust, until you hand it over to CalPERS. He also mentioned if
you’re underfunded why not just give the money straight to CalPERS right away.

Member DeLarme mentioned that his understanding of the purpose of a Trust is to
segment assets so they cannot be used for other purposes by future City Councils. Chair
Greenberg mentions the purpose is to restrict that funding so it’s always there for
pension debt versus general operations or capital or whatever else.

In response to Chair Greenberg’s request, Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi addressed the
Committee. The intent and discussion with the City Council Pension Ad-Hoc
Committee and full City Council was that the 115 Trust was a holding tank for money
that would eventually be handed over to CalPERS.

Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi mentioned that in a previous year the
IPAC did look into having a trust account with another vendor other than PARS like
CAMP. She mentioned PARS is not the only vendor to handle 115 Trusts, compared to
CAMP, the IPAC before did not like PARS. Member DeLarme wondered if the 115
Trust is a pressing issue now or if it can be put on the back burner for now. Chair
Greenberg responded that residents are concerned about the growing pension debt and
that as City Government we should address their concerns. Chair Greenberg mentioned
that the idea of the trust would be one part of the strategy for pension obligations.
Another option could be a pension obligation bond. Part of the discussions the Chair has
heard (with Council Members) was how does the City manage and insure that we are
paying at least what we are currently incurring with CalPERS, don’t let the debt get big.
The City is currently paying the minimum amount due, not the full cost we incur on an
annual basis. The City pays the normal cost, somewhat less than the real cost, and a
portion of the liability which initially applied to interest. Chair Greenberg mentioned
that the growth of the pension debt is alarming to Council and residents.

In conclusion, the Subcommittee didn’t hear bad things regarding Section 115 Trusts,
however the Subcommittee is not sure how this would fit into the City’s strategy for
debt management. Member DeLarme mentioned that he is willing to do more research,
it would be City Council’s decision to see if this needs to be explored further. It is
unclear right now how the 115 Trust would be part of the strategy to handle pension
debt.

ACTION: Moved by Member DeLarme, seconded by Member Murdock to
(1) Allow minutes to reflect the discussion in regards to the 115 Trust and the Report
of the Subcommittee Members DeLarme and Murdock; and (2) Forward the minutes
to the City Council for their information.
AYES: Greenberg, DeLarme, Murdock
NOES: None
   RESULT: Motion Passed.

3.  Annual Review of the City of Palos Verdes Estates Investment Policy

  Recommendation Action: Receive a Report from Staff and the Chair, Review the City of
  Palos Verdes Estates Investment Policy, and Make Recommendations to the City
  Council as Deemed Appropriate.

  Chair Greenberg presented.

  Chair Greenberg mentions that this review process should be done annually and ideally
  during the budget cycle for the next fiscal year. No recommendations for changes for
  Fiscal Year 2021/2022. The Chair, as City Treasurer, is allowed to delegate authority to
  Staff to make investment decisions, execute transactions and not sure if we have had
  this process done before. The Chair questioned was there ever a formal delegation of
  authority drafted to allow anyone on Staff (City Manager Guglielmo and/or City Support
  Services Director Stephen Hannah) or to the City Council the ability to make investment
  decisions or execute transactions? Mr. Cole responded no such delegation has been
  made to his knowledge, that it is common to have a delegation of authority in cases of
  emergencies or in much larger organizations if the treasurer is so busy or there were so
  many transactions it may warrant the treasurer to have a “right arm.” Good provision to
  have in case of an emergency. Chair Greenberg asked if this formally needs to be
  presented at a meeting. Mr. Cole responded: if the City Treasurer is delegating, then it
  is an individual action a Treasurer can do and recommended any such delegation should
  be done in writing formally, the Treasurer’s signature should be notarized.

  The Chair opened a discussion with regard to portfolio yield. One of the objectives is to
  retain a market rate of return and references to a benchmark for the City’s portfolio’s
  performance. Is there somewhere precisely stating the market rate of return that the City
  should follow. Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi answered that there wasn’t anything specific in
  the Investment Policy. Theoretically, different durations have different benchmarks.
  Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi mentioned that it is vague and not defined in the Investment
  Policy. Member DeLarme doesn’t recall setting a benchmark in the Investment Policy
  but says it should be on the to-do list for updating the Investment Policy.

  The Chair posed a second question for consideration by the Committee: assignment of
  the custodial services for the City’s portfolio. Chair Greenberg announced that Union
  Bank has sold its Custody Business to US Bank and as of late summer US Bank will be
  taking it over. We can keep our current representatives (April B.). Ask if there is
  anything formal we need to do to appoint them, if they assumed all the assets and
  liabilities. Member DeLarme mentioned that the Investment Policy has a Broker
  Certification, but this is a custodian so he is not sure if we have such a thing. Mr. Cole
  added that US Bank is a successor in interest of the City’s existing contractor and the
  City resulting from a transaction between Union Bank and US Bank. The City played
  no part in the transaction and clarified that no members of the City staff, including City
  Council Members, did not participate in the transaction. Mr. Cole added: We should
   check to make sure we don’t need US Bank to perform a certification in accordance with
  the Investment Policy. Chair Greenberg mentioned that normally the acquiring company
  assumes the contract and the obligations of the contract. Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi asked if
  US Bank grandfathered the fees. Mr. Cole answered at least for the time being, they
  would honor the fees. Chair Greenberg mentioned they did talk about it and there would
  be no increase in fees. Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi mentioned the fees are super cheap and
  we should hang onto them for as long as we can.

  Chair Greenberg mentioned that we are required annually to review our broker dealers.
  A couple have been with us for a long time and the two new ones that (former City
  Treasurer) Liz Ying brought in are very recent and she is certain that Ms. Ying
  completed tons of due diligence. Member DeLarme confirmed, Ms. Ying met with Piper
  and Sandler. He mentioned they reviewed their certification documents and was signed
  off on. Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi asked if we have to get a formal Brokers Questionnaire
  annually. Chair Greenberg responded: yes. The Chair asked if action can be to check the
  record of when we did the recertification/certification of the brokers.

  Member DeLarme asked if there were any updated or changes in respects to government
  codes that needed to be included in the Investment Policy. Mr. Cole responded that staff
  has looked into it and no updates or changes have been made to the relevant sections of
  the Government Code.

  ACTION: Moved by Member DeLarme, seconded by Member Murdock to approve the
  Investment Policy of the City of Palos Verdes Estates without amendment and
  recommend approval of the Investment Policy to City Council.
  AYES: Greenberg, DeLarme, and Murdock
  NOES: None
  RESULT: Motion Passed

  AMENDED ACTION: Amended by Chair Greenberg, seconded by Member Murdock
  to amend Section 18 of the Investment Policy of the City of Palos Verdes Estates to
  reflect City Council’s action to have four members from the public appointed by City
  Council in addition to the City Treasurer as Chair to the IPAC.
  AYES: Greenberg, Murdock, and DeLarme
  NOES: None
  RESULT: Motion Passed

4.  Discussion of a Portfolio Investment Strategy with Focus on Targets for Various
  Investment Terms

  Recommendation Action: Receive a Report from Staff and the Chair and Make
  Recommendations to the City Treasurer as Deemed Appropriate.

  Chair Greenberg presented.
 The Chair is seeking the Committee’s feedback on what the City’s investment goals and
strategies should be.

Member DeLarme asked if there is any type of current holding statement or aggregation
of our investment position so that we could give opinions on if we should go out further
on the yield curve or adjust our credit quality.

The Chair brought up the March City Treasurer’s Quarterly Report and noted we
needed to do some number crunching regarding liquidity. She mentions just because
you need liquidity doesn’t mean it all has to be in a money market account or in LAIF.
Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi asks how much money is in LAIF at the end of March. Chair
mentions there is $14.6 million in LAIF. Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi responded that such a
balance in LAIF seemed high and the City should do something with it. Member
DeLarme mentioned that with the information at hand, why would the City go out five
years. He mentioned the City should do some due diligence before moving a couple of
million dollars around. Member DeLarme also mentioned contacting the City’s
brokers and see what they recommend. He asks the Chair if they have given any
feedback and the Chair responds that they have been great. She mentions that she has
made some investments that were four to five years at 140, 130 basis points yield. The
Chair mentioned she doesn’t know what will happen in five years but at least some of
the portfolio is invested at a higher rate than LAIF. The Chair mentions one potential
investment that recently arose was the pension obligation bond for the City of
Manhattan Beach. Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi asked if we can buy a pension obligation
bond. The Chair responded that if the credit quality is there then the coupon is going to
be higher because of the taxable nature of the bond. Member Murdock mentioned that
he is not comfortable buying pension obligation bonds, we already have our own risk
to pensions, now were buying someone else’s risk to pensions. Not sure we want to
compound our risk like that. Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi asked if a pension obligation bond
is a general obligation of the issuer. Member Murdock responded that it is. The Chair
mentions that gets Cities in trouble because instead of paying CalPERS they invest it
in something else. Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi responded than when you issue a pension
obligation bond, you have to hand the money over to CalPERS. Member Murdock
asks what the term on the pension obligation bonds. The Chair responds that she didn’t
recall the specific term and Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi added that it won’t be five years.

Member DeLarme asks if there is a way to have the transactions sent to the
Committee. The Chair responded yes. Member DeLarme mentions the template Ms.
Ying and Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi had pie charts in them so they could see the weighted
maturity duration, vitality, etc. of the portfolio. Member DeLarme suggested to have
another meeting with Member Boyd present, with more information so the Committee
can give better guidance in terms of positioning. He is not comfortable loading up on a
particular investment or leaving it in LAIF until he has more information. Mayor Pro
Tem Lozzi mentions that they should have a meeting when they have a new member.
   The Chair mentioned that the Investment Policy states that the IPAC consists of two
  members not four. City Clerk Chaney responded that there was an error on the list,
  there are two openings for IPAC members. City Clerk Chaney mentioned when the
  City Council amended the IPAC membership last year, it was expanded from two
  members to four. There are two openings for terms that start July 1st. City Clerk
  Chaney mentioned that when Member Murdock was appointed, there were no other
  applicants. He was appointed to a one year term so the terms would be staggered since
  the other members terms were up as well. This leaves the other two new members with
  full two year terms.

  The Chair suggests that the Committee have another meeting to decide what our
  portfolio strategy should be. If we can’t meet until July, then she is not comfortable with
  all that money in LAIF. The Chair mentioned that there are a lot of items in the City’s
  investment portfolio that are subject to call and all that gets deposited in LAIF absent
  any other direction. Member Murdock ask if everything has gotten called by now. He
  mentioned it should have happened by now. The Chair mentioned she has been trying
  to purchase new investments with more call protection. She also mentioned that the
  brokers have been great, she looks at what they send every day and if there is something
  really good in there then she’ll buy $250,000 or $500,000. Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi added
  that the good thing about the agencies is that you can pick up a million bucks of those,
  you can buy them in bigger chunks. She says it’s hard to buy $250,000 at a time when
  you’re trying to put $12 million dollars to work.

  The Chair suggests another meeting to further the discussion and have the new member
  included. Mr. Cole suggested another meeting in July. Kylynn mentions the next
  meeting for IPAC is July 20th.

  ACTION: Moved by Chair Greenberg, seconded by Member Murdock that the IPAC
  reopen the discussion of investment portfolio strategy at the next meeting July 20th and
  in the meantime, if something very attractive comes along, she will invest prudently and
  judiciously in trying to reduce the balance in LAIF.
  AYES: Greenberg, DeLarme, and Murdock
  NOES: None
  RESULT: Motion Passed

5.  Discussion of Potential Future Agenda Items

  Recommendation Action: Discuss Proposed Future Agenda Items and Provide
  Feedback to the Chair as Deemed Appropriate.

  Chair Greenberg asks the IPAC if there were other topics that should be discussed at the
  next meeting. Mr. Cole suggested that for the July 20th meeting as a standing item, the
  Quarterly Investment Report goes to the IPAC before going to City Council for
  approval. The Chair and Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi voiced agreement.
